messages:
Ashley: heads-up — saw a large uptick in kv evictions on gpu-7 during the longctx canary run, correlates with p99 token latency blips.
Ashley: logs show sustained eviction bursts once seq_len > 1200 and memory step-up beyond expected.
Dennis: eviction or fragmentation?
Ashley: eviction count mainly, but fragmentation metric (pages_per_key) moved right too. snippet: 
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] kv: evict=410 freed_pages=168 compaction_fail=2 residency=0.58
[2026-03-18T09:12:18Z] kv: insert=5200 prefix_miss=0.47 reuse_hit=0.09 memory_bytes=13.8GB
```
Katie: 13.8GB sounds high for that host/model mix. any change in keying recently?
Ashley: yes — tenant_beta pushed a change that appended session_id to the cache key for a short-lived UX flag last week.
Liam: so cardinality exploded and we stopped seeing cross-request prefix reuse?
Ashley: exactly. unique_keys_per_minute jumped from ~1.9k -> ~8.5k in the window. hot prefixes got evicted in favor of large per-request KV blobs.
perf-bot: perf-regression detected: p99-token-latency +7ms on gpu-7 coincident with kv-evict-rate +3.2x.
Dennis: immediate mitigation options: rollback session_id from key; add per-request thinpool reservation so longctx requests dont push out global hotset; or cap prefetch/allocation per-request.
Katie: thinpool looks attractive as short-term. we can expose operator config for reservation size per-host or per-queue.
Liam: streaming fallback for oversized requests is doable but will spike tail latency; prefer canonicalizing keys first (strip ephemeral fields).
Ashley: spun a canary build that normalizes keys for tenant_beta only, results were promising — unique_keys dropped ~68% and eviction rate returned close to baseline.
Ashley: proposed normalization config (canary):
```
kv.key_normalization:
  enabled: true
  tenant_overrides:
    tenant_beta:
      strip_components: ["session_id", "debug_id"]
      max_prefix_len: 192
```
Dennis: we should also add a lightweight compactness sampler. sample every 15k ops and compute pages_per_key and unique_keys spike. if above threshold trigger either compaction or allocate thinpool.
Liam: will prototype thinpool allocator. idea: reserve N% of pages for longctx_pool and do not evict from short_prefix_hotset into that reserved region. operator-configurable.
Katie: on observability: add charts for unique_keys_per_minute, pages_per_key_p50/p95, avg_pages_per_request, and host-level "hotset_retention" metric. alert if unique_keys > baseline*2.5.
Ashley: also noticed mem growth over longctx sessions — per-request KV grew steadily and only reclaimed after compaction run. we should enforce a soft per-request page-ttl so ephemeral per-request keys expire faster (e.g., 30s) unless marked shared.
Dennis: agree. soft-ttl + normalization + thinpool should be a good multilayer defense. we also need tests that simulate interleaved short+long workloads.
Liam: I'll add a deterministic unit/integration test for hotset retention: simulate 90% short prefix traffic + 10% longctx bursts and assert hotset_retention >= 0.8 after sustained burst.
Katie: I'll add dash tiles and a muteable alert rule (so canary noise doesn't spam #pager).
Ashley: quick canary timeline: normalized keys at 09:20, eviction fell by ~65% within 10 mins, p99-token latency reverted.
perf-bot: regression alert auto-muted after canary key normalization applied.
Dennis: next steps:
1) roll key normalization behind feature flag to other tenants with similar UX flags
2) land thinpool prototype (Liam) + e2e tests
3) implement compactness sampler + compaction trigger
4) add soft-ttl + operator knobs for per-request cap
Katie: I'll draft alert thresholds and dashboard PR.
Ashley: I'll write a short postmortem and link the canary graphs. sync Fri 10am to triage longer-term policy (prefetch throttling vs streaming). ping @everyone if you want to join. :eyes:
